 Saba Ali Khan Opens Up About Her Father’s Final Moments, Saif-Amrita’s Separation, And More
 Saba Ali Khan Pataudi, sister to actors Saif Ali Khan and Soha Ali Khan, in a recent interview talked father Mansoor Ali Khan Pataudi's demise, sibling Saif, his separation, and more. 
 Author: Aarti Tiwari 
 Published: 07 Nov,2026 10:00:56 PM 
 Saba Ali Khan Pataudi, sister to actors Saif Ali Khan and Soha Ali Khan and a successful jewelry designer, sat down for a rare, deeply personal interview on the Siddharth Kannan YouTube Channel. During the interview, Saba talked about her father’s death, her brother’s public separation from Amrita Singh, and more.
 Abba’s Last Breath 
 When Siddharth asked about the most emotional moment for the Pataudi family, Saba named the passing of her legendary father, Mansoor Ali Khan Pataudi. She shared that during his last breath, all the members were together as a family. Saba emphasized that the memory remains an incredibly raw space for the family, one that never fails to evoke tears and deep nostalgia.
 On Heartbreaks And Relationships 
 Saba shared that she has never experienced a romantic heartbreak because she has never actually had a first boyfriend. She disclosed that when she was 18 or 19, she was introduced to many people to marry, but none worked out because she couldn’t find anyone who measured up to the standard set by her father.
 Despite remaining single, Saba said she is still completely open to finding love at this stage of her life. She emphasized that she is looking for someone who can be a friend and someone she can have a mutual conversation with.
 Saif AliKhan’ss Break-up With Amrita Singh 
 Addressing the highly publicized 2004 divorce between her brother Saif Ali Khan and actress Amrita Singh, Saba recalled, “I was in Delhi at that time studying, while they were living in Mumbai.”
 She said she felt deeply sad for Saif, noting that he and Amrita looked wonderful together and had two beautiful children, Sara and Ibrahim. She emphasized that a marital separation of that scale invariably takes a massive emotional toll on an individual.
 The Paparazzi Culture Surrounding Nephew Taimur 
 Speaking about this, Saba admitted she finds it unsettling that the young boy is tracked all over the internet. She also shared that she criticized a friend who once claimed to be a huge “fan” of Taimur. She questioned how any adult could genuinely be a fan of a four-year-old child. Calling the mass obsession “unnecessary,” Saba reiterated the need to protect young star children from constant public exposure.
